# EXE-BM002-01 — PNG review audit

**42 review images.** Every one was generated by `review_views.py` from the
reference's own B-rep solids and every one was opened and looked at. This file
records what each shows, whether it is legible, and whether it may be used as
review evidence.

* Source geometry signature: `6824e5102424e3db883f16b684ab54f02c14eed19bead0116c704092156bc2ee`
  — asserted before the first image is drawn and re-asserted after the last.
* Renderer, 3-D views: `cadvideo.rasterise` — a true z-buffer over per-FACE
  tessellations. Triangles carry shading only; only a face's own rim is stroked,
  depth-tested against the finished buffer.
* Renderer, sections: `cadval.section_polygons` walked into filled, hatched
  patches. Orthographic, cut faces only, nothing behind the plane drawn.
* Tessellation deflection 0.4 mm. Output 1600 × 900 px.
* No generative image model was used. No proxy, redrawn or substituted geometry
  appears anywhere.

**Inspection method.** 24 images were opened at full resolution during the
generate–inspect–fix loop (listed as `full-res` below). The remaining 18 were
opened together as a 700 px-wide contact sheet after the final regeneration
(`sheet`), which is enough to confirm framing, body colouring, state, arrow sense
and annotation placement, and each of those 18 is one of a series whose sibling
was inspected at full resolution. Four images were re-opened at full resolution
after the last annotation fix.

**Display cutaways.** Where an image says a body is *cut* or *removed*, the solid
was intersected with a half-space, or omitted, **for display only**. The model is
never modified — the signature check after the run is what proves it. Every such
image says so on its face.

All cut faces are filled **and** hatched, with a distinct hatch per body, and
nothing behind the plane is drawn. Every section is orthographic.

**Why the detail panels exist.** A 0.2 mm clearance on a 150 mm-wide section is
about one pixel. A section without an enlargement cannot be evidence for the fit
it is supposed to show. Every fit quoted in the packet is enlarged in a panel on
the same sheet as the section it comes from.

Frames 01, 05 and 09 carry **KINEMATIC EXTREMUM — NOT A VERIFIED PHYSICAL HARD

## 7. Classified DELETE_AND_REGENERATE

**None in the current set.** Six defects were found by inspection during this
phase and every one was corrected by regenerating, not by relabelling:

1. **B-B kept the wrong half.** The cutaway kept x < 30, which deleted the crank
   arm and left the Ø70 hub in its place, so the image showed a disc where the
   crank should be. Now keeps x > 30 and the arm is exposed. *(This was a
   defect in the image, not in the CAD.)*
2. **Operation rotation arrow reversed** — see §5.
3. **Guide clearances unreadable.** The first C-C was a full-width section in
   which 0.2 and 0.4 mm are sub-pixel. Rebuilt with three detail panels,
   including a plan cut, because the side clearance is not visible in the
   x = 33 plane at all.
4. **Journal clearances unreadable** — same problem in A-A; two detail panels added.
5. **Rear panel invisible in the body-identification view.** It sat behind the
   housing, so its leader pointed at nothing. It is now lifted 88 mm off.
6. **Label collisions** — banner over header, leaders over the colour key, inset
   labels off the frame edge, a leader pointing at a guide channel the cutaway
   had removed. All repositioned.

No image was kept that a reviewer would have had to be told how to read.

## 8. The twelve required questions

**1. Can the external user input be located?**
Yes. `review_overall_front_iso.png` (labelled, with the rotation arc),
`review_overall_left.png` (face-on, grip sweep drawn), and
`review_external_crank_user_interface.png` left panel. It also appears outside the
housing in every assembly frame from `review_assembly_02_crank_shaft_inserted.png`
onward, and in `review_internal_mechanism_cutaway_iso.png` in the same view as the
linkage it drives.

**2. Can the 26 mm handle radius and the 45 mm internal crank radius be told
apart?** Yes. `review_external_crank_user_interface.png` puts them in two panels
side by side, each dimensioned, with a text block saying they are two features of
one body and that no gearing relates them. The 45 is dimensioned again in all
three `review_section_BB_*` images and in
`review_internal_mechanism_rear_panel_removed.png`; the 26 again in
`review_overall_left.png`.

**3. Can the complete crank-to-platform chain be followed?**
Yes. `review_kinematic_chain_annotated.png` names all ten elements with feature
IDs and writes the chain out. `review_section_BB_crank_link_platform_mid.png`
shows crank arm → pin → rod → platform joint → platform in one uninterrupted
picture with both dimensions on it. Items hidden behind the hub in those views are
cut open in `review_section_AA_shaft_and_dual_journals.png`.

**4. Can both housing-side shaft journals be understood?**
Yes. `review_section_AA_shaft_and_dual_journals.png` shows land 1 (x 0–8, and it
is also the boundary crossing), the relief (x 8–14) and land 2 (x 14–26), each
labelled **BODY-HOUSING**, with DETAIL 1 enlarging 0.2 / 3.2 / 0.2 so the reader
can see that the two lands are two and not one long bore. The same sheet states
that the rear panel carries no shaft journal, and the panel is drawn on it.

**5. Can the overhung crank-arm arrangement be understood?**
Yes. `review_section_AA_...` labels it directly — *"OVERHUNG CRANK ARM x 30–40,
both journal lands are on its −X side"* — and the geometry on that sheet shows the
arm standing beyond both lands with nothing beyond it.
`review_section_BB_*` shows the arm itself with the hub cut away.

**6. Can both joint pins and their axial retention be understood?**
Yes. `review_section_DD_crank_joint_retention.png` and
`review_section_EE_platform_joint_retention.png` each show the pin in its bores,
the head seated on the face that stops it going one way, and the rear-panel land
2.0 mm from the head end that stops it going the other, with the measured free
travels quoted. Both sheets state the land is integral to the panel and that there
is no circlip, washer or screw in the product.
`review_assembly_07_rear_panel_approach.png` shows both lands arriving.

**7. Can both platform guides be understood?**
Yes. `review_section_CC_platform_guides_bottom / _mid / _top.png` — the same plane
and scale at all three states, with DETAIL F, DETAIL B and the DETAIL S plan cut
carrying the three clearances (0.2 side, 0.4 tip, 0.4 plate edge).

**8. Can platform motion from bottom to top and back be understood?**
Yes. The nine `review_operation_*` frames tabulate crank angle against support
height through a full turn and mark the two reversals as kinematic extremes rather
than stops. `review_section_BB_*` gives the same three key states as measured
drawings.

**9. Can payload access be understood?**
Yes. `review_section_FF_payload_access_bottom.png` and `_top.png`: the aperture at
the rim, the envelope descending, and the arrow **ending on the platform support
surface**, with the 98 mm and 8 mm rim-to-surface relations dimensioned and the
capacity caveat on the sheet.

**10. Can the assembly sequence be understood?**
Yes. The nine `review_assembly_*` frames, each with the real insertion direction
arrowed, the pins installed before the panel, and the panel's two lands shown
arriving behind the two pin heads.

**11. Can a reviewer identify all seven product bodies?**
Yes. `review_body_identification.png` numbers all seven with leaders, and a colour
key appears on every 3-D image.

**12. Can a reviewer distinguish the scenario payload from the product bodies?**
Yes. It is drawn in a distinct grey, keyed as **PAYLOAD (SCENARIO)**, and labelled
**SCENARIO OBJECT — NOT A PRODUCT BODY** in
`review_body_identification.png`, in every operation frame, and in both F-F
sections, where it also carries **1 KG SCENARIO DECLARED / STRUCTURAL CAPACITY NOT
VERIFIED**.

---

## Conclusion

**YES — READY FOR INDEPENDENT HUMAN CAD REVIEW**

All twelve questions are answered by named images. No image in the set is
classified MACHINE_ONLY or DELETE_AND_REGENERATE. The six defects found during
inspection were fixed by regenerating the images; none required a change to the
CAD, and the geometry signature is unchanged at
`6824e5102424e3db883f16b684ab54f02c14eed19bead0116c704092156bc2ee`.

What these images do **not** establish: strength, stiffness, crank effort,
jamming, safety, manufacturability, assembly force, wear or life. Every image
says so on its face.
